acceptance: Plain Verify passes on a sealed, untampered ledger and still fails on a tampered live line (test)
A byte-identical carry re-proves on a sealed ledger (ship test through carrySatisfied)
VerifyDeep inside Seal's truncate-then-anchor window does not report ErrSealResidue for a seal in progress (test)
docs/plans/ledger-restructure-2026-10.md lists this item as a hard prerequisite of C12 and C13
fix: Make plain Verify segment-aware enough to verify a sealed ledger: start the strict walk from the newest segment's anchored tail hash. That is the ledger plan's C12 (incremental verify); land it, or this narrower fix, before C13 seals anything on the plane. Give Seal one atomic step: append the anchor before releasing the chain lock, or have VerifyDeep treat a segment whose anchor is the next append as in-flight. Pin both with tests: seal then plain Verify, seal then carrySatisfied, and VerifyDeep inside Seal's gap.
source: console, 2026-10-07 re-review of the carry lane (finding A4)
summary: Found by the 2026-10-07 re-review of the carry lane (dev/cl-carryf5, finding A4), pre-existing. After a seal, the first live line chains from a line that now lives in a sealed segment, so plain Verify reads only the live file and stops with 'line 0 chained-genesis prev_hash mismatch' on every sealed ledger (the package doc's open finding). Ship's carry check, carrySatisfied, runs that live-only Verify, so the first seal of the plane ledger would make every byte-identical carry fall back to a re-audit, for good. Separately, Seal truncates under the lock and appends its segment_seal anchor only after releasing it; a VerifyDeep inside that gap reports ErrSealResidue (no anchor for the segment) although nothing is damaged. A reviewer probe in the carry lane's scratch (TestProbeRereview_VerifyInsideSealsGap) shows both.
title: Sealing the ledger makes live-only Verify fail for good, which would disable every carry; Seal's gap also shows ErrSealResidue to a concurrent VerifyDeep
